key_insight: Scale-driven averaging attenuates uncertainty in panel ultimate load, while spatially correlated interface variability remains essential for predicting early damage initiation and location.
engineering_relevance: Match uncertainty-model complexity to the design criterion: spatially uniform variability for global capacity and correlated random fields for local damage in aerospace skin–stringer bonds.
method: Extend likelihood-free Bayesian calibration from Mode I to Mode II using experimental coupon data.
Propagate interface variability from coupons to panels using simulation-based stochastic finite elements.
Compare industrial B-basis, spatially uniform variability, and spatially correlated random-field approaches.
evidence_signal: Coupon experiments support stochastic parameter identification, and panel simulations indicate uncertainty attenuation in ultimate load but sensitivity of early damage to local weak spots.
watch_item: The abstract does not report quantitative accuracy or panel-scale experimental validation, so applicability beyond the studied configurations needs verification.
paper_title: Scaling of Interface Variability in Aerospace Composite Structures: A Multi-scale Stochastic Approach from Local Identification to Panel Response
